builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Lara Mini Base: Language Diversity as a Resource, Not a Trade-off
summary: Lara Mini Base replaces the standard dense multilingual base model with a Mixture of Experts architecture (7.2B total, 0.6B active parameters) to mitigate capacity competition between languages. It costs the complexity of serving an MoE model and memory for 7.2B parameters (approximately 14.4 GB in bfloat16, leaving limited headroom on a 24 GB GPU for the 128k context KV cache), while adoption is further restricted by the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 non-commercial license. Potential failure modes include underperformance in languages outside its 45 supported languages, long-context memory exhaustion, and degradation on tasks requiring alignment tuning since this is a base model.
rationale: The model fits on a single 24 GB GPU and claims state-of-the-art quality for its active-parameter class, but its non-commercial license and unvalidated real-world performance require workload-specific testing before production adoption.

claims.statement: Lara Mini Base replaces the standard dense multilingual base model with a Mixture of Experts architecture (7.2B total, 0.6B active parameters) to mitigate capacity competition between languages. It costs the complexity of serving an MoE model and memory for 7.2B parameters (approximately 14.4 GB in bfloat16, leaving limited headroom on a 24 GB GPU for the 128k context KV cache), while adoption is further restricted by the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 non-commercial license. Potential failure modes include underperformance in languages outside its 45 supported languages, long-context memory exhaustion, and degradation on tasks requiring alignment tuning since this is a base model.
For a single user on one GPU, without quantization, it generates text at least 1.8 times faster than any model with a higher average score.
